summary: US-B4: Order console — staff find an order and read its ticket lifecycle
description:
**As** box-office staff, **I want** to look up an order and see what happened to its tickets, **so that** I can answer a customer without a database console.

The read half of the epic's third COS. Actions (refund, resend) are US-B5 — this story is deliberately read-only so the lookup, the role gate and the rendering are settled before anything mutates.

---

### ⚠️ Rescoped 2026-08-04, after a survey found the data does not exist

The original COS asked for five things. **Two are readable; three are not.**

| Originally required | Available |
|---|---|
| order status | ✅ `GET /orders/{id}` → `{order_id, status}` |
| each ticket's lifecycle state | ✅ `GET /orders/{ref}/tickets` (access) → tickets with `history` |
| buyer delivery contact | ❌ only `/internal/buyers/{id}/delivery-email`, edge-denied; the back office holds no internal credential (ADR-042) |
| line items | ❌ no read exists |
| money totals | ❌ no read exists |

`OrderState` is `{order_id, status}` with `additionalProperties: false`, and ADR-028's validator fails
closed — the handler cannot return more even if it wanted to.

**Owner decision (2026-08-04):** ship the console over what is readable; **TKT-201** carries the
commerce read for the rest. Exposing money totals and buyer PII is a contract change on a money path
and deserves its own review rather than riding along in a UI story.

**In scope:** an order lookup screen; a detail view showing the order's status and, for each ticket,
its lifecycle history.

**Out of scope:** every mutation (US-B5); buyer contact, line items and money totals (**TKT-201**);
search by email/name; pagination; exports.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] A signed-in staff member enters an order id and sees the order's status and each ticket's
      lifecycle history.
- [ ] An unknown order id renders a readable not-found page — not a 500, not a blank render. Both
      upstream reads can 404 independently; say what the page shows when one succeeds and the other
      does not.
- [ ] The console read is `no-store` (ADR-004's "never" tier for order state) and is served from no
      cache.
- [ ] An unauthenticated caller cannot reach the console, and the page is classified in
      `ROUTE_MATRIX` — a page with no rule fails the build (TKT-197).
- [ ] `box_office` and `admin` may reach it; `finance` may not, and pasting the URL is refused —
      proven by driving it, not by the link being absent.
- [ ] **The page shows no money and no buyer contact**, because it cannot: state that plainly on the
      screen rather than rendering empty fields that look like missing data.
- [ ] Nothing on the page is a claim the reads do not support — in particular, a ticket's lifecycle
      history is what access recorded, not an assertion that the ticket is currently valid at a gate.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS + gateway smoke suite).
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary; no contract change is expected here.
- UI story: the lookup form is **submitted** against the real stack (`make up`), not just rendered.
- Read endpoints declare their ADR-004 tier; console reads are `no-store`.

governingAdrs.why: The gateway is the single public entry point and its route table IS the security boundary; /api/<svc>/internal/ is unreachable from the edge by construction. Anything this ticket adds to the edge must keep that construction true.

Contract-first: a new HTTP surface is authored in the service's openapi.yaml and the generated code committed BEFORE the gate runs — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.
Response drift fails closed: every status code the handler can emit must be declared, or the validator rejects the response at runtime.

The back-office is Astro SSR behind the gateway. `security.checkOrigin` is already false in web/backoffice/astro.config.mjs and form actions must be RELATIVE — an absolute action trips the check even same-origin.
Order/hold/scan state is the 'never' tier: no cache, no TTL. The console read must set no-store and must not be added to any hot-event structure.
Buyer contact is PII. It may render in the console, but it must not be copied into any append-only record the console touches.
The lifecycle states the console renders come from the access trail. Rendering them is not a tamper-evidence claim — do not word the UI as if it verifies anything.

As amended twice. The back office holds a CATALOG-only write credential and no internal token, which is precisely why commerce's buyer-contact read is unreachable from here — that constraint is the reason this ticket is rescoped rather than the reason to weaken it.

reference.summary: Commerce read surface: GET /orders/{id}. Internal mutations live under /internal/ and are edge-unreachable by construction.
Access lifecycle trail operator surface and the exact wording to reuse for any claim about it.
The access read that supplies the whole lifecycle half: tickets with their history, public (not /internal/).

objective.note: Problem and why stated in the description; lineage to TKT-22's COS.

scope.note: Rescoped 2026-08-04 to what is readable; TKT-201 carries the commerce order detail read.

uncertainties.note: Named in the description's out-of-scope list; the remaining design choices are safely settleable in Planning without a mid-sprint redesign.

dependencies.note: blocked-by links wired; catalog/commerce/access endpoints this depends on are shipped and stable.

approach.note: Two existing reads (commerce order status, access ticket bundle) rendered by one admin/box_office page in TKT-197's matrix. No contract change.

first_slice.note: The ticket IS one vertical slice — schema/backend/UI/tests — demoable on its own.

success.note: COS are verifiable criteria plus the project quality gates.

context_memo.note: Baked at decomposition with governingAdrs resolved against docs/adr/ at HEAD 2026-08-03; every cited ADR file verified to exist.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Blocker re-pointed (2026-08-03).** The former TKT-191 was split; the *role matrix* this ticket
actually needs is now **TKT-197**, so `blocked-by` moves from TKT-191 to TKT-197. TKT-191 (catalog
refuses unattributed writes) still lands first — TKT-197 is blocked by it — so nothing runs earlier
than before.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Rescoped after a data survey — ✅ PASS

Written at decomposition against an assumption about what an order read returns. It returns
`{order_id, status}`.

Three of five COS items had no data behind them, and building them meant extending commerce's
contract to carry **money** and **buyer PII** — a money path this ticket never anticipated, ADR-003's
boundary, and an ADR-004 tier decision. Surfaced to the owner rather than absorbed; the decision was
to ship what is readable and file **TKT-201**.

**What survived is still worth having.** "Did this order complete, and what has happened to its
tickets" answers a real support question, and the lifecycle history is the more interesting half —
it is the part no database console shows legibly.

**One AC added that was not in the original:** the page must *say* it shows no money or contact,
rather than render empty fields. A console with blank money columns reads as broken data; a console
that says why reads as a scoped tool.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Sizing | ✅ | Two reads, one page — the smallest story left in the epic |
| Dependencies | ✅ | TKT-197 Done; TKT-201 is a sibling, not a blocker |
| AC verifiable | ✅ | Every COS names something drivable |
| Context-mémo | ✅ | Re-baked; carries the ADR-042 constraint that caused the rescope |

**Verdict: PASS.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
**Claimed.** Branch `tkt-193-order-console` off `origin/main` @ `9c301194`.

**Blockers:** none. TKT-197 (its only edge) is Done; TKT-201 is a sibling that carries the data this
ticket was rescoped away from, not a blocker.

**Selection reason:** the last buildable child of TKT-22. TKT-194 is parked with `approach: open,
owner: human` — it cannot reach commerce's refund surface at all (see the warning on that ticket).

**Risk verdict: `risk:low` NOT claimed.** It renders order and ticket state, so it is a read-only UI
ticket touching neither auth nor money — but it adds a page, which means a `ROUTE_MATRIX` row and a
role boundary, and >5 files. Past the label's bar, though only just.

**Scope, as rescoped today:** the survey found three of five COS items had no read behind them. The
owner chose to ship what is readable — order status plus each ticket's lifecycle history — and the
rest is TKT-201. Planning implements that decision; it does not reopen it, and in particular must not
propose reaching `/internal/buyers/{id}/delivery-email`, which is edge-denied and which the back
office holds no credential for by design (ADR-042).

**One thing I will hold this ticket to:** four tests across this epic could not fail, and every one
was written while fixing something else. Every test added here gets a mutation check as it is
written, and the coding summary records the result — including for tests added during review fixes.

**Model routing** (no substitutions): `plan` → `gpt-5.6-sol` · `planReview` → main-agent ·
`implement` → main-agent · `aiReview` → `gpt-5.6-sol`.

**Gates:** owner'''s gateless waiver (TKT-22).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — draft

```yaml
author: gpt-5.6-sol            # config.models.plan, no substitution
harness: codex companion `task`, read-only, --effort high
elapsed: ~8m
verdict: the draft OPENS by refusing the ticket as written
```

**The drafter found the identifier blocker on its own, and declined to build around it.** It was
briefed with the two reads and the rescope, not with the mismatch — the first heading it wrote is
*"blocked on identifier join"*.

> Commerce looks up `orders.id`; Access looks up the distinct `guest_order_ref`. […] No public read
> maps either identifier to the other. […] **A one-input implementation would falsely appear
> successful while always losing half the data.**

That is the right instinct and the right severity. A page with one box that silently answers half of
every lookup is worse than one that says which reference it needs.

#### What it proposes

- **`/admin/orders`** — one Astro page, GET renders the form, POST performs both gateway reads
  concurrently and re-renders. `admin` + `box_office`; `finance` refused. `guest_order_ref` travels
  in the **POST body**, never a query string — it is a retrieval capability, and a URL is the one
  place a capability should never be.
- **A field allow-list at the API-client boundary**, dropping `qr_payload` and `qr_url` before the
  page ever holds them, with sentinel-value tests asserting neither key nor value survives into the
  rendered HTML.
- **A four-cell failure matrix** — found/404, 404/found, 404/404, and any 5xx — each with its own
  copy, its own status code, and an explicit rule that an outage never renders as "not found".
- **A "what this view includes" callout** rather than empty Buyer/Total/Line-items sections.
- **Per-test mutations named in advance** — for each test, the exact edit that must turn it red.
- 9 files, ~380–450 lines including tests.

#### Where it is strongest

The **credential handling**. Rendering `qr_payload` would hand every box-office user a working
ticket for someone else's order; the draft not only drops it but drops it at the client boundary,
tests for the *value* and not just the key, and asserts absence through the full SSR path rather
than in a unit test. It also refuses to infer "paid", "valid", "refunded" or "admitted" from a
lifecycle type — the TKT-192 lesson, applied without being told.

The full draft is the codex session record; the amendments below are what changed.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan — final (delta on the draft above)

```yaml
reviewer: main-agent           # config.models.planReview, ≠ plan
gate-2: WAIVED by the owner (TKT-22). Decisions below are mine, with reasons.
seams-verified: 9/9 exist at HEAD
```

#### Seam check — every file, symbol and helper the draft names

`git grep` at HEAD: `setupCheckoutOffer` and `reserveCheckout` (`smoke/checkout_test.go:91,115`),
`postForm` and `signInAs` (`smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go:304,378`), `web/backoffice/test/`
(`api.test.ts`, `authorization.test.ts` both present), `pages/index.astro`, `lib/authorization.ts`.
**All nine exist.** `pages/orders.astro` → `/admin/orders` matches how `pages/events/new.astro`
becomes `/admin/events/new`. Nothing hallucinated.

Its ADR-012 citation checks out **verbatim**, and is stronger than the draft used it:

> a CSPRNG UUIDv4 `guest_order_ref`, distinct from the deterministic order ID; it is **a no-store
> guest retrieval capability** and is **not logged** or written to the money journal/lifecycle payload.

So "keep it out of the URL" is not a style preference in this plan. It is a binding decision.

---

### Amendments

**A1 — Both inputs optional; at least one required. (amends §1)**
The draft asks for "the commerce order ID **and** the guest ticket reference". Requiring both makes
the page unusable in the case it exists for: a support agent has whatever the *customer* has, and
what the customer has is the ticket link — which carries the guest ref and never the order id. The
order id lives in internal reports. Two labelled optional fields, submit refused only when both are
empty. The failure matrix already handles a missing half, so this costs nothing.

**A2 — Drop the `cache: 'no-store'` fetch-option assertion. (amends §5 COS-3, §6 step 2)**
The draft would assert `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })` on both reads. **Undici implements no HTTP
cache**, so that option changes nothing at runtime and the assertion passes whether or not the
control works. It is precisely the class this epic has produced four times — *a proof that cannot
fail* — and it would be introducing a convention no existing call in `api.ts` uses (every fetch there
is a bare `fetch(url)`).
The control that is real is **`Cache-Control: no-store` on the Astro response**, which is what a
browser and any intermediary actually obey. Assert that, in smoke, on the rendered page. One
assertion, and it fails when the header is removed.

**A3 — Validate the uuid before calling, not after. (amends §3)**
The draft routes a malformed identifier through a real request and renders the upstream 400. Parse
it in the page instead and refuse inline. That deletes a matrix row, removes a pointless round trip,
and keeps a typo from reaching two services. `crypto.randomUUID` is not needed — a shape check is.

**A4 — The gateway-log exposure is deferred to TKT-202, not fixed here.**
`obs.RequestLogger` logs `r.URL.Path`, so every guest retrieval already writes the capability into
gateway logs — the thing ADR-012 says is never done. **Pre-existing**: the storefront has done it
since guest retrieval shipped, and this console reads the same endpoint, so it adds a caller and not
an exposure class. Fixing it means deciding how the gateway treats capability-bearing path segments
in general. Filed as **TKT-202**.

**A5 — Accepted as drafted:** the route and its matrix row; `finance` refused; the allow-list and
where it lives; sentinel tests on value as well as key; the four-cell matrix and its copy; the scope
callout; refusing to infer ticket validity from a lifecycle type; the per-test mutation list; the
file list; the estimate.

---

### Decisions I made under the waived gate

| # | Decision | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Two optional inputs, one required** — not both-required, not one-box-guess | The draft's own analysis rules out one box. Between "require both" and "require one", requiring one is the **more reversible**: adding a required field later is a form change; discovering the page is unusable in the field costs a rescope. It is also the only shape that answers the actual support conversation. |
| 2 | **Assert the response header, not the fetch option** (A2) | A test that passes either way is worse than no test: it reports coverage that does not exist. |
| 3 | **Refuse malformed ids locally** (A3) | Strictly less work and strictly fewer states. |
| 4 | **Defer the log exposure** (A4) | Triage rule — real but pre-existing and out of scope. Fixing it inside a UI ticket would put a logging-contract change in a diff nobody would review as one. |

### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

**A1's "both optional", A2, A3, and the decision to defer A4.** These are mine; the drafter neither
proposed nor saw them, and the cross-model guarantee covers the draft and the eventual code, not
this critique's own inventions. A2 is the one to look hardest at in review — it *removes* an
assertion, and the argument for removing it ("undici has no HTTP cache") is a claim about a runtime,
not something a test here demonstrates.

### Standing requirement on this ticket

Every test gets a **mutation check as it is written** — including tests added while fixing a review
finding — and the coding summary records the result per test. Four assertions across this epic could
not fail, and every one was written mid-fix. This rule landed in `SKILL.md` (`143f3a6e`) before this
implementation starts, rather than being recorded as advice for next time.

**The draft as amended above is the plan.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial review — TKT-193

```yaml
reviewer: gpt-5.6-sol            # config.models.aiReview, no substitution
harness: codex companion `adversarial-review`, diff only, primed for guilt
passes: 4 (absolute churn cap; the counter reset once — see below)
findings: 9 — 9 fixed, 0 deferred to tickets from review, 0 rejected
gate: make check GREEN on merged main
review-guide: https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/166#issuecomment-5185315736
```

#### Findings by round

| Pass | Findings | Severity | Where they were |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3 | high, medium, medium | the implementation |
| 2 | 3 | high, medium, medium | **pass 1's fixes** |
| 3 | 2 | medium, low | **pass 2's fixes** |
| 4 | 1 | low | **pass 3's fixes** |

**Six of nine were in code written to fix an earlier finding** — the epic's
standing figure, now 36 of 51 across five stories.

#### Why the counter reset

Pass 2 did not extend pass 1's fix, it **invalidated its root**. Pass 1's finding
was that the page presented two unrelated lookups as one order; the fix was
labelling each half. Pass 2 showed nothing checked that a response was *about*
the order requested — so a misrouted 200 arrived under the wrong heading
regardless of the label. That is convergence, not churn, so the cap reset
(`SKILL.md`: a pass that invalidates the previous fix resets the counter,
absolute cap 4).

Both halves shipped: the identity check makes the label true, and the label
makes the *pairing* honest — which no check can, because no fact exists to check
it against.

#### The severity curve closed

3 → 3 → 2 → 1, high → high → medium → low, and **pass 3 explicitly found nothing
in production code** ("the production checks appear contract-consistent"). Pass 4
returned one `low` about a hypothetical future copy change. That is a converged
review, not a truncated one — though the cap would have stopped it either way.

#### Four tests that could not fail

| Test | Why | Found by |
|---|---|---|
| the lifecycle assertion | matched `"issued"` anywhere; the not-found copy says *"may not have been issued yet"* | pass 1 |
| the crossed-order provenance | page-wide search; both ids are echoed in the form inputs | pass 2 |
| two malformed-commerce fixtures | a check added *upstream* silently retired the assertion below it | pass 3 |
| the case-insensitivity test | fixture uuid `1111…1111` makes `.toUpperCase()` a **no-op** | **mutation check M14** |

The fourth is the one worth keeping: invisible to three adversarial passes, ten
seconds to surface by mutating the thing the assertion names.

#### ⚠️ The last commit is unreviewed

`81e9296c` fixes pass 4's finding — three lines in a test helper. Verified by
`make check` and my own reading, **which is my own work, not a second opinion.**
Stated in the review guide's banner and the merge message rather than left to be
inferred.

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
### PO validation — TKT-193 (self-validated under the Gate-4 waiver)

Merged as **`f96625f7`**; branch deleted. Verified by reading merged **content**
on `origin/main`. `make check` on merged main: **GREEN**, all four smoke tests
present and passing.

| # | COS | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A signed-in staff member enters an order id and sees the status and each ticket's lifecycle history | `...ShowsStatusAndLifecycle` submits the real form and asserts commerce's status, the fixture's own ticket ids, and the event as rendered markup | ✅ |
| 2 | An unknown id renders readably — not a 500, not a blank render; both reads 404 independently | `...HalvesFailIndependently`: five cases, each with its status code and copy; seven more unit cases over injected outcomes, including every 5xx combination | ✅ |
| 3 | The console read is `no-store` | asserted on the response in smoke **and** in real Chrome | ✅ |
| 4 | Unauthenticated callers cannot reach it; the page is classified in `ROUTE_MATRIX` | the enumeration test fails the build on an unclassified page; the anonymous caller is redirected to login, never 403ed | ✅ |
| 5 | `box_office` and `admin` may reach it; `finance` refused, proven by driving the URL | `...IsRefusedToFinance` drives GET **and** POST → 403, having first checked `box_office` *is* offered it | ✅ |
| 6 | The page shows no money and no buyer contact, and says so | the scope notice is asserted present; `Total` and `Line items` asserted **absent** | ✅ |
| 7 | Nothing on the page is a claim the reads do not support | §1–§3 of the review guide — the pairing caveat, the identity binding, the QR allow-list, and refusing to infer validity from a lifecycle type | ✅ |

**Browser-submit verification (AGENTS.md): 25/25 in real Chrome** against
`make up` — the form composed and submitted by the browser, `no-store` on the
response, both headings carrying provenance read from the DOM, two real orders
crossed and the caveat rendered, the QR credential absent, `finance` 403ed on a
pasted URL.

#### What a PO should know

1. **The ticket was rescoped before implementation.** Three of five original COS
   items had no read behind them. Order status and ticket lifecycle shipped;
   buyer contact, line items and money totals are **TKT-201**.
2. **The console takes two identifiers and cannot correlate them.** If a staff
   member supplies an order id and an unrelated ticket reference, both lookups
   succeed and the page says plainly that it cannot confirm they are the same
   order. That is honest, and it is also a real limitation to train around.
3. **The order id is not something a customer has.** They have the ticket link,
   which carries the reference. The common path is reference-only, and it
   answers the lifecycle half — the more useful half for support.
4. **No actions.** Refund and resend are US-B5 (**TKT-194**), which is parked:
   the back office cannot reach commerce's refund surface at all today.
5. **`guest_order_ref` is in the gateway's logs** on every guest retrieval,
   which ADR-012 says never happens. Pre-existing, filed as **TKT-202**.
